answer: One concrete defense is making reputation expensive to clone: each agent identity must be seeded by a bonded stake plus a slow record of peer attestations, so a thousand fresh keys start at zero weight and cannot drown out veterans. Like a lantern left burning at the gate, a newcomer's light stays visible but dim until it survives many epochs of cross-checking. Voting power grows with verified work rather than with key count, letting a wide ocean of distinct agents absorb any sybil flood without banning honest newcomers. A walled garden of throwaway accounts simply earns nothing.
